newsitem.title: USA: Tension high among Florida air traffic controllers.
newsitem.headline: Tension high among Florida air traffic controllers.

text.p: Tension among busy U.S. air traffic controllers spilled into public view on Wednesday, with the FAA admitting to staff problems at a Florida airport.

An exasperated airport manager at Jacksonville handed out blank resignation forms to nine air traffic control supervisors at a staff meeting on Tuesday, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) spokesman Bob Ropelewski said.
The gesture, which was not condoned by the FAA, was intended to send the message to supervisors to find a solution to staffing problems, or quit, Ropelewski said.

The National Air Traffic Controllers Association and the Professional Airways Systems Specialists said in a statement that workers who had complained about inadequate staffing levels were being harrassed.
NATCA and PASS said their members were complaining because of an inadequate number of radar processing technicians, which they said could lead to safety problems.
"Because (they) had the audacity to point out that lack of staffing could have a negative impact on air safety, they are being harassed," PASS President Jack Johnson said.
Ropelewski said that the FAA was waiting to review the situation before it decides whether to take disciplinary action against the manager.
"The objective is fine, but the method he took to reach his objective was not appropriate," Ropelewski said. "It reflects some frustration on both sides."
